rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 7 (base_speed 1.6, with the iteration 6 geometry and gains) is the best raced design at 219.96, up from 173.5. The oval finished 6 of 20 runs, against 2 of 20 at base_speed 1.4. Oval progress rose from 0.74 to 0.76, and s-bend progress rose from 0.32 to 0.36. Speed is therefore converting oval near-finishes into completions, and completions carry 500 points each. Line loss stayed at about 1.0 per run on every track, as in every raced iteration, so the speed change did not make line loss worse. The oval mean finish time (1.975 s) did not fall as 1/speed would predict, but the time term is worth at most 60 points, so completions dominate the score.

The Evaluator's stated rule for this case is: if oval completions rise and the score exceeds 173.5 with progress held, keep base_speed and try a further step to 1.8 in one step. Both conditions are met (score 219.96, oval completions 6, progress held or rising). The entityR1 approval of the 1.6 design was written before it raced, so it is treated as background only.

Change. Raise controller.base_speed from 1.6 to 1.8. This is the only change. Geometry (outer sensors at x = ±0.04, y = 0.05; inner three at y = 0.03; sensor_size 0.012) and all gains (kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], line_loss last_direction) are kept, so the result reads cleanly against 219.96.

Expected result. More oval completions (target 8 or more of 20) and a score above 220. Risk: a faster robot leaves the 0.06 m off-track limit sooner on the s-bend and slalom, so s-bend progress may fall below its current 0.36. Revert rule: if oval progress falls below about 0.70 or s-bend progress falls below about 0.30, return base_speed to 1.6 and test controller.ki at 0.15 to address line loss.

Hypotheses. (a) Speed 1.8 gives more oval completions, because the finish-time margin under the 3.0 s cap is still limited. (b) Line loss stays near 1.0 whatever the speed, so turn-in lag, not speed, is the cause of off-track endings on the s-bend and slalom. Measurements wanted: completion, completion_time, progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, to see whether the off-track limit becomes the binding constraint at this speed.
